title: No identity-bound reflective invocation for heterogeneous typed callables
summary: Profile 0.18 supports host invocation by module/function name and explicit generic type arguments, but it does not expose a bounded identity-bound invocation membrane that validates a compiler callable identity and heterogeneous typed argument material without consumer-specific dispatch generation.
requiredBehavior: Expose a fail-closed generic invocation surface accepting an authoritative exported callable identity, interface/signature identity, typed argument material, and applicable generic arguments while preserving capability admission and returning a bounded typed result.

observation.summary: The current typed-call ABI resolves module/function targets and explicit generic type arguments, while declaration-inventory exposes stable callable and signature identities. The runtime has no identity-targeted heterogeneous typed invocation surface; mncs-test still requires transparent generated selector dispatch.

reproduction.instructions: run the current host-generic entrypoint conformance and inspect the declaration-inventory-to-provider path; the named module/function route passes, but no callable-identity plus typed-material route exists

evidence.summary: Named generic entrypoints with explicit type_arguments work across declared backends.
The provider still generates identity matchers and static calls because callable identities cannot be invoked directly with heterogeneous typed signatures.

workaround.description: mncs-test generates native provider_inventory.mncs from the compiler declaration inventory; the generator is transparent typed glue, not semantic test policy.
